title_as_printed: Comparison of Calorimetric and van't Hoff Delta H0 for Solution of Gaseous Hydrocarbons into Water at 35 C (printed with a degree sign and -Delta H0 headers)

footnotes_as_printed.a: This work. Uncertainty is twice the standard deviation of the mean. Units: kJ-mol^-1.
footnotes_as_printed.b: Olofsson et al., Ref. 26. Uncertainty is twice the standard deviation of the mean.
footnotes_as_printed.c: Rettich et al., Ref. 21. Uncertainty is twice the standard deviation as calculated according to the method of Clarke and Glew.
footnotes_as_printed.d: Wilhelm et al., Ref. 18. Uncertainty is twice the standard deviation as calculated using an equal temperature interval data set, Ref. 4, based on the method of Clarke and Glew.

pressure_note: standard-state enthalpy of solution; gas partial pressure = measured total pressure minus water vapour pressure, then transformed to standard state with second virial coefficients (as stated in text); no pressure column

value.what: standard enthalpy change of solution dH0 of the gas in water; printed column is -dH0 (positive), so scale -1; calorimetric, this work

uncertainty.what: twice the standard deviation of the mean

composition.other_species: pure water, gas at infinite dilution (standard state)

skip_rows.reason: gas label rows (gas name printed beside the first data row, written as its own label row)

extra_unmapped: -dH0 c (Rettich et al. Ref. 21, van't Hoff from solubility, from_literature) and its uncertainty
-dH0 d (Wilhelm et al. Ref. 18, van't Hoff, from_literature) and its uncertainty
notes: Each printed gas row has the value line and an uncertainty line below; written as one data row with separate +- columns. Printed ± sign omitted. Gases outside the seven (neopentane, cyclopropane, ethene, propene, 1-butene, ethyne, butanes) kept. Temperature written as 15 C / 35 C in title; scale not stated.
